vignette: A 70-year-old man has a stroke leaving him unable to see anything in his right visual field, but he can still recognize faces and read slowly. His pupils react normally. On fields, a small island of central vision survives on the right.
stem: Where is the lesion and why is the center spared?

options.text: Right optic tract; the macula has bilateral representation
Left calcarine cortex; the occipital pole receives middle cerebral artery collateral supply
Left optic radiation; macular fibers run separately
Left lateral geniculate; the macula projects to the pulvinar
Right calcarine cortex; the field defect is functional

explanation: A congruous right hemianopia with normal pupils is a left calcarine (PCA) infarct, and the spared central island is macular sparing, because the macular cortex at the occipital pole is also supplied by terminal middle cerebral artery branches.
